slot.brief: Graph of [A] vs t or concentration ratio; ask how many half-lives elapsed for a given concentration drop (first order).

stem: For a first‑order reaction, the concentration of the reactant decreases from $0.8\ \text{M}$ to $0.1\ \text{M}$. The number of half‑lives that have elapsed is

verdicts.working: The concentration changes by a factor of 0.1/0.8 = 1/8 = (1/2)^3, so 3 half-lives have elapsed.

working:
Fraction remaining = 0.1/0.8 = 1/8 = (1/2)³. Therefore 3 half‑lives have passed.

Independent check: The concentration changes by a factor of 0.1/0.8 = 1/8 = (1/2)^3, so 3 half-lives have elapsed.
solution:
After $n$ half-lives, the fraction remaining is $(1/2)^n$.
$$\frac{0.1}{0.8}=\frac18=\left(\frac12\right)^3$$
Hence, $3$ half-lives have elapsed.
